note: Task 7 steps 2-4 (generate/post-process/mockup) for the starter biome terrain tileset. PixelLab job ids, placement rules and the bit convention actually observed from each get_tiles_pro result.

bit_convention.rule: corner (arity 4), mask = NW<<3 | NE<<2 | SW<<1 | SE
bit_convention.pixellab_placement_rules_say: a set bit means the FIRST listed terrain (item 1 in the numbered description) occupies that corner
bit_convention.since_item_1_is_always_the_floor_descrip: bit=1 in the raw PixelLab tile index means FLOOR at that corner -- same as the spike (maskBit: 'lower')
bit_convention.pack.py_stores_upper_mask: 15 - fileIndex, so file tile_0 (0000, no floor corners) -> stored key '15' (all four corners upper/rock), file tile_15 (1111, all floor) -> stored key '0' (no upper corners, pure floor)
bit_convention.verified_visually: cropped art/tiles/starter/pack/terrain.png at manifest positions for rock mask '0' (pure dusty floor), mask '15' (solid dark rock), mask '8' (rock in NW corner only), mask '1' (rock in SE corner only) -- all matched the NW<<3|NE<<2|SW<<1|SE convention exactly

spend.note: Round 1: 2 of the 8 jobs (both floor-variant style-mode attempts) were unusable failures; still within budget. Round 2 (user-requested fixes): 2 more jobs (bridge_h, bridge_v standalone rerolls), ~$0.19, within the ~$0.20 approved.

bridge_h_reroll.tool: create_tiles_pro (shape mode, single item, standalone -- no batch)
bridge_h_reroll.description: 1). rickety wooden plank-and-cable bridge spanning horizontally, seen from directly above, planks and rope only, no moss, no ground, isolated
bridge_h_reroll.picked: tile_5.png -- clean vertical plank fence pattern (planks perpendicular to travel direction, correct for a horizontally-spanning bridge), no green moss fringe this time.
bridge_h_reroll.cutout: sides=top,bottom only (tolerance 12, default) -- the plank subject is DESIGNED to reach the left/right edges (so it tiles along its span axis); trusting all 4 border sides as background would (and initially did) eat the planks themselves, since their colour touches the left/right border ring. Result: 26.7% of the tile made transparent (the sky sliver at top, gravel sliver at bottom).

bridge_v_reroll.description: 1). rickety wooden plank-and-cable bridge spanning vertically, seen from directly above, planks and rope only, no moss, no ground, isolated
bridge_v_reroll.note: Inconsistent job: most of the 16 tiles came out with the SAME vertical-plank orientation as the bridge_h job (wrong), only a few (tile_9, tile_10, tile_14, tile_3) showed the correct perpendicular horizontal-rung look. Tried tile_3 with cutout sides=left,right, but its background was too close in colour to gaps between the planks and ~87.5% of the tile (most of the subject) was eaten.
bridge_v_reroll.final_choice: Abandoned the generated bridge_v tiles entirely. bridge_v is conceptually bridge_h rotated 90 degrees, so the ALREADY-CUTOUT bridge_h.png was rotated 90 degrees with PIL (Image.ROTATE_90) to produce bridge_v.png -- same clean art, guaranteed-consistent quality, no extra spend.

cutout_tool.algorithm: samples the outer border ring (default all 4 sides, overridable via --sides), clusters its colours in Lab space, flood-fills border-connected pixels within a Lab-distance tolerance of those clusters to alpha=0, then feathers a small bounded ramp (default 1px) at the cut boundary on the KEPT side only (no whole-image blur -- that was tried first and ate too far into small subjects).

per_tile_tuning.hazard: tolerance=12 (default), sides=all -- 62.0% of tile made transparent
per_tile_tuning.exit: tolerance=4 (lowered from default 12) -- the stone archway frame is close in Lab tone to the floor background at tolerance=12 and was getting eaten along with the true background; at tolerance=4 the frame survives and only the genuine floor-coloured corners are cut. 47.2% of tile made transparent
per_tile_tuning.torch: tolerance=12 (default), sides=all -- 66.5% of tile made transparent
per_tile_tuning.bridge_v: derived by rotating the cutout bridge_h.png -- no separate cutout run needed

NOT applied to stamps (hazard/bridge/exit/torch keep their own accent colours per the earlier R3 ruling).

round3_user_fix_exit_reroll.reason: User feedback on round 2: the exit archway's INTERIOR (the black doorway opening) was transparent after cutout because it touched the tile border (bottom/left edges), so the floor/wall art behind the stamp showed through the hole -- read as a free-floating arch outline, not a doorway.
round3_user_fix_exit_reroll.root_cause_confirmed: inspected the round-2 stamps_cutout/exit.png alpha channel directly (ASCII alpha map): the curved top arch frame was opaque, but the entire lower interior/threshold region was alpha=0 -- exactly the reported bug, not a misdiagnosis.

variant_1_rectangular.description: 1). top-down view of a dark cave passage doorway: a worn stone threshold framing a deep black opening that recedes into darkness, the opening fully filled with black/near-black void, isolated, no surrounding ground
variant_1_rectangular.verdict: rejected -- a plain rectangular stone block with a black window, reads as 'a wall segment', not distinctly as a doorway/exit marker at 48px.

variant_2_archway.description: 1). top-down view of a stone archway tunnel exit, a worn stone doorframe with a faint arrow scratched into its threshold, the doorway itself completely filled with solid black void leading into the tunnel beyond, isolated, no floor or ground around it
variant_2_archway.verdict: picked -- gothic-arch silhouette reads immediately as a doorway/tunnel mouth. Picked tile_4 (warm umber-grey stone tone, matches the palette better than the cooler tile_0/1, clean render, no artifacts).

round3_user_fix_exit_reroll.void_border_check: for BOTH new jobs, scanned every border-ring pixel of several candidate tiles for Lab L < 8 (near-black): 0 hits in all of them. Unlike the round-2 tile, this prompt's 'isolated, no surrounding ground' framing made the model paint the void fully enclosed within the frame (never reaching the tile edge) -- so this specific reroll doesn't even reproduce the original failure mode. keep_dark_l was still applied as a deliberate safety net per the brief (defence in depth, not load-bearing for this particular tile).
round3_user_fix_exit_reroll.background_removal_finding: the border ring for the picked tile is 100% frame/stone material (L ranges smoothly 15-59 across the ring, one continuous shaded surface, no separate flat 'background' cluster at all) -- the 'isolated, no surrounding ground' prompt made the model fill the WHOLE 24x24 canvas with stone, not just an inset archway on a plain backdrop. Tried tolerance 12/6/3 with cutout: every setting ate progressively more of the frame itself (natural stone-shading variance lets the flood fill step from shade to shade across the whole material), down to unrecognizable fragments at tolerance>=3. There is no tolerance that removes 'background' here without also removing the frame, because there is no separate background in this art to find. Settled on tolerance=1 (near-inert -- only the few most extreme corner-noise pixels get cut, ~4% of the tile) + keep_dark_l=10: frame fully intact, arch silhouette clean, void solid opaque black, only cosmetic corner speckle removed.

keep_dark_option.behaviour: a pixel with Lab L at or below keep_dark_l is NEVER classified as background, regardless of its Lab distance to a border colour cluster and regardless of whether it touches the border -- overrides the normal distance test.
keep_dark_option.selftest: new fixture: light-grey background (L~60) with a near-black void (L~6) that intentionally touches the bottom border, mirroring the exact doorway-to-darkness case. Without keep_dark_l: void probe alpha = 0 (bug reproduced). With keep_dark_l=15: void probe alpha = 255 (fixed). Background probe alpha with keep_dark_l active = 0 (confirms real background is still cut normally, not over-protected). All existing selftest checks still pass; full `SELFTEST PASSED`.

round3_user_fix_exit_reroll.mockup_context: exit sits at grid (x=10, y=6) in the unchanged 12x9 hand-authored room, one cell in from the east wall column (x=11) -- already 'a floor cell at the room's edge next to wall' per the brief; no grid change was needed. Cropped and re-inspected in the rebuilt _mock.png: reads clearly as a stone archway with a solid black tunnel mouth set into the room's edge next to the rock border.

round4_user_fix_cleanalpha.reason: User feedback on round 3: exit reads better, but sloppy/flakey cutout edges on the stamps -- caused by the tolerance=1 cutout nibbling stray edge pixels, and the (then-default) 1px feather ramp leaving semi-transparent fringe pixels, which reads as anti-aliased blur rather than a clean pixel-art cut.
round4_user_fix_cleanalpha.spend: $0 -- pure post-processing, no PixelLab generation calls this round.

cleanalpha_tool.added: scripts/tiles/postprocess.py cleanalpha() (+ CLI subcommand `cleanalpha`), plus a `_connected_components` 4-connected flood-fill labeller it shares with nothing else (kept private/local to this pass).
steps: 1. binarize alpha at threshold 128 -> every pixel becomes 0 or 255, no partial values survive

2. remove stray opaque specks: 4-connected opaque components smaller than min_speck=3px, other than the single largest opaque component (always kept as the main subject regardless of its own size), are cut to transparent

3. fill small enclosed transparent pinholes: 4-connected transparent components smaller than min_hole=3px that do NOT touch the tile border (interior holes, not real surrounding background) are filled opaque, coloured by the mean RGB of their immediately-adjacent opaque rim pixels
cleanalpha_tool.cutout_integration: cutout() now calls cleanalpha() at the end by default (clean=True param, opt-out via --no-clean on the CLI). DEFAULT_CUTOUT_FEATHER changed from 1 to 0 -- the feather ramp is what produced the semi-transparent fringe pixels the user flagged; it's now off by default and purely opt-in, with cleanalpha as the intended way to tidy an edge.
cleanalpha_tool.selftest: new fixture: a 16x16 subject square with (a) a feathered ramp just outside its edge in BOTH directions of the threshold (alpha 64 and alpha 180 on opposite sides), (b) 3 isolated 1-2px opaque specks in the background, (c) a 2px enclosed pinhole inside the subject. After cleanalpha: 0 non-binary alpha pixels remaining (PASS), all 3 specks removed (PASS), pinhole filled (PASS), every other subject pixel unchanged (PASS). Full suite still `SELFTEST PASSED` (all round 1-3 cutout/grade/match checks unaffected).

stamps_reprocessed.hazard: re-ran cutout(raw/stamps/tile_2.png) with the new defaults (feather=0, clean=True) -- 0.0% partial-alpha pixels remaining (was nonzero under the old feather=1 default)
stamps_reprocessed.torch: re-ran cutout(raw/torch_supp/tile_2.png) with new defaults -- 0.0% partial-alpha remaining

stamps_reprocessed.bridge_v: re-derived as the freshly-cleaned bridge_h.png rotated 90 degrees (PIL Image.ROTATE_90, an exact pixel permutation, no interpolation) -- 0 non-binary alpha pixels confirmed directly
